Reproductive output in Tule perch is partitioned into discrete broods, with gravid females typically containing between 15 and 25 embryos per pregnancy. The combination of a small clutch size and infrequent reproduction means that annual reproductive output is concentrated into a single, high-quality cohort of fully developed juveniles. This strategy maximizes per-offspring investment and likely enhances survival during the critical post-parturition period, when the young must rapidly acquire exogenous feeding skills in the shallow, structured habitats of the Sacramento River delta.
